tasks.title: Remove name field from `islamic_prayer_times` config flow
tasks.body:
The `islamic_prayer_times` integration includes a name field in its config flow schema. Config flows should not ask users to provide a name. The name is either derived from discovery or from the integration manifest.

Remove the name field from the config flow, per the `hass-config-flow-name-field` pylint rule.

Part of home-assistant/epics#47, which contains more information, including migration instructions.

tasks.title: Fix swallowed exceptions in dlna_dmr action handlers
tasks.body:
The `dlna_dmr` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `media_player.py`:**
- `async_media_next_track` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_pause` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_play` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_previous_track` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_seek` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_stop` (media_player.py)
- `async_mute_volume` (media_player.py)
- `async_play_media` (media_player.py)
- `async_select_sound_mode` (media_player.py)
- `async_set_repeat` (media_player.py)
- `async_set_shuffle` (media_player.py)
- `async_set_volume_level` (media_player.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

tasks.title: Home Assistant Signal Messenger integration does not trigger push notifications for "Note to Self"
tasks.body:
**Configuration**
```
notify:
  - name: signal_name
    platform: signal_messenger
    url: "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
    number: "+49XXXXXXXXXX"
    recipients:
      - "+49XXXXXXXXXX"
```
**Problem**

When sending a message to my own Signal account ("Note to Self") using the Home Assistant notify.signal_name service:

✅ The message is delivered successfully.
❌ No push notification is shown on the phone.

**Comparison**
Using Home Assistant Signal integration
```
action: notify.signal_name
data:
  message: "Test"
```

Result:

Message arrives in Note to Self but ❌No push notification.

Using the REST API directly
```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "message":"Test",
    "number":"+49XXXXXXXXXX",
    "recipients":["+49XXXXXXXXXX"],
    "notify_self":true
  }' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8080/v2/send
```
or
```
rest_command:
  signal_name:
    url: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v2/send"
    method: POST
    headers:
      Content-Type: application/json
    payload: >
      {
        "message": {{ message | tojson }},
        "number": "+49XXXXXXXXXX",
        "recipients": ["+49XXXXXXXXXX"],
        "notify_self": true
      }
```
Result:

Message arrives in Note to Self and ✅Push notification is received

If I send the same request with `"notify_self": false` the message is delivered but ❌no push notification is generated.

**Conclusion**

The REST API behaves correctly and supports notify_self.

The Home Assistant signal_messenger integration appears to send self-messages without enabling notify_self (or uses an API endpoint that does not support it), resulting in messages that arrive but do not generate a push notification.

Could the integration be updated to support notify_self (or otherwise preserve the previous behaviour for self messages)?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2028.8.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2028.7.4

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

signal messenger

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/signal_messenger

_No response_

```yaml
configuration.yaml:

    url: "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
    number: "+49XXXXXXXXXX"
    recipients:

Automation:
```

tasks.title: Cover toggle OpenGarage cover toggle fails
tasks.body:
### The problem

Calling `cover.toggle` on my OpenGarage entity frequently results in a silent failure. The garage door does not respond to the toggle and there are no associated error logs. Running `cover.close` works just fine, and HA always has the correct state of the garage door (open or closed), so it's not confused about the door state.

This seems to be somewhat time dependent: if I haven't used HA to open the garage in a while, `cover.toggle` is likely to fail. But once it starts working, it works consistently for some period of time (hours) before it starts to fail again.

I've looked through the implementations of [cover](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/cover) and [opengarage](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/opengarage), and there's one thing I find suspicious. The cover toggle code was https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/59233 to only [toggle closed if the last toggle direction was open](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e19c6ac0118f81a2b2b5a8e9ab6f741c48c064ee/homeassistant/components/cover/__init__.py#L442).

This matches my experience of having much more trouble toggling closed than toggling open (I can't recall if toggling open is a problem). But I can't deterministically trigger the bug based on this logic, i.e., by toggling the cover closed, then manually opening outside of HA, then trying to toggle closed again. I don't understand how integrations store state such as `self._cover_is_last_toggle_direction_open` over time, possibly there's some time-based aspect to how this is updated.

tasks.title: SMTP does not recognise image attachments generated with action: camera.snapshot
tasks.body:
### The problem

Images generated by action: camera.snapshot are not recognised as images when attached to email notifications. as a result they are attached as application/octet-stream instead of image/jpeg.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

SMTP

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/smtp/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
action: notify.mail_sender
data:
  message: Doorphone Motion Detected
  data:
    images:
      - /config/www/snapshots/doorphone.jpg
```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
WARNING [homeassistant.components.smtp.helpers]
Attachment /config/www/snapshots/doorphone.jpg has an unknown MIME type. Falling back to file
```

### Additional information

Root cause
homeassistant.components.smtp.helpers.py _attach_file() does:

  attachment = MIMEImage(file_bytes)

which raises:

   TypeError: Could not guess image MIME subtype

for valid JPEGs.

The JPEG starts:

ffd8fffe00104c61766336322e32382e31303200...

i.e. JPEG SOI followed by a COM marker containing:

Lavc62.28.102

The file is valid and opens correctly with other applications.

Workaround
Fallback using mimetypes:

try:
    attachment = MIMEImage(file_bytes)
except TypeError:
    ctype, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(atch_name)
    if ctype and ctype.startswith("image/"):
        attachment = MIMEImage(
            file_bytes,
            _subtype=ctype.split("/", 1)[1],
        )
    else:
        attachment = MIMEApplication(
            file_bytes,
            Name=os.path.basename(atch_name),
        )

In addition, the warning text is slightly misleading. The MIME type is known (image/jpeg from the filename); the problem is that MIMEImage cannot infer the subtype from the binary data. That distinction will probably help avoid people chasing the wrong cause.

tasks.title: Fix swallowed exceptions in huawei_lte action handlers
tasks.body:
The `huawei_lte` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `notify.py`:**
- `send_message` (notify.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

tasks.title: Recorder purge_entities does not purge history for group.* entity_id (group states remain untouched)
tasks.body:
### The problem

When calling `recorder.purge_entities` with `entity_id` containing a `group.*` entity, Home Assistant does not delete any rows for that group entity from the `states` table. The group entity has its own entry in `states_meta` and a very large number of `states` rows, including rows older than the requested retention period. The purge task runs and deletes rows for other entities, but never targets the group’s `metadata_id`, so the group’s history remains unchanged.

This appears to be caused by group expansion during entity_id processing, where the group entity_id is expanded to its members and the group entity_id itself is not included in the purge target set.

`components / recorder / services.py / _async_handle_purge_entities_service(...)` generates the list of entities by calling `homeassistant.helpers.service.async_extract_entity_ids(service)` and leaves `expand_group` parameter to the default value, which is `True`:
`async def async_extract_entity_ids(service_call: ServiceCall, expand_group: bool = True) -> set[str]:...`

tasks.title: enphase_envoy: transient uint32-max (2^32 Wh) consumption readings permanently corrupt long-term energy statistics
tasks.body:
## The problem

The Envoy consumption CT occasionally returns a transient garbage reading of
~`4294967296` Wh (exactly uint32 max) for daily consumption. The
`sensor.envoy_<serial>_energy_consumption_today` entity (kWh,
`total_increasing`) then reports a state of ~`4,294,629 kWh` for one update
cycle before returning to normal (~hundreds of kWh).

Because the statistic is `total_increasing`, the recorder treats the spike
as real consumption and bakes ~4.29 million kWh into the statistic's
cumulative `sum` **permanently**. When the counter drops back, HA treats it
as a normal counter reset, so the spike is never reversed. Each occurrence
adds another ~4.29e6 kWh step. The Energy dashboard and any consumer of the
consumption statistic are unusable afterwards without manual DB surgery.

## Evidence (from my recorder DB, HA 2026.7.2)

All spike deltas cluster at 2^32 Wh = 4,294,967.296 kWh (minus the real
consumption in the hour):

| Serial | spike events | example event (local time) | hourly `sum` delta (kWh) | baked-in error (kWh) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 202442014493 | 2 | 2025-05-05 08:00 | 4,294,684.702 | 8,576,091 |
| 202504003374 | 18 | 2025-08-19 21:00 | 4,294,963.763 | 77,304,135 |
| 202428004328 | 1 | 2025-12-16 10:00 | 4,294,356.343 | 4,294,356 |
| 482543015950 | 1 | 2026-05-31 00:00 | 4,294,629.126 | 4,294,629 |

Example raw statistics rows (serial 482543015950, metadata_id 5651):
state jumps `276 → 4,294,629.126 → ~277` in adjacent hours; `sum` steps up
by 4,294,629 and stays there for every subsequent row (897 rows and
counting).

Four different Envoy serials (hardware swaps) all exhibit it, across
three firmware builds in the 8.3 line (8.3.5167, 8.3.5286, 8.3.5289) — it is a device/firmware artifact, not a
one-off. Notably the **lifetime** (MWh-scaled) statistics from the same
device are clean; only the "today" Wh-scaled consumption endpoint produces
the uint32-max readings.

## Suggested guard

The integration (or pyenphase) should reject physically implausible values
before they reach the state machine, e.g.:

- Reject/skip an update where daily consumption ≥ 2^32 − ε Wh (a sentinel
  for a failed CT read), or
- Reject deltas that exceed a plausible bound (e.g. >1 MWh change in a
  single poll for a residential "today" counter), returning the previous
  value / marking unavailable for that cycle.

Precedent: other energy integrations clamp or drop known firmware sentinel
values rather than publishing them into `total_increasing` statistics,
because a single bad publish is unrecoverable without manual statistics
surgery.

## Environment

- Home Assistant Core 2026.7.2 (recorder on SQLite)
- Integration: `enphase_envoy` (core)
- Hardware: Envoy metered w/ consumption CTs + Enpower/IQ batteries;
  4 serials over the install's life (RMA swaps): 202442014493,
  202504003374, 202428004328, 482543015950 (current)
- Firmware (per serial, from HA device registry): 202442014493 + 202504003374 = 8.3.5167; 202428004328 = 8.3.5286; 482543015950 (current) = 8.3.5289

## Diagnostics

Happy to attach integration diagnostics and the raw statistics rows for the
spike windows on request.

tasks.title: Derivative Sensor is marked Unavailable after each midnight until a second sample is received that day
tasks.body: ### The problem I realise there was MUCH discussion in the past about how to calculate and show 0 rate of change when Home Assistant only reports changes of data. I believe this is fixed for almost all cases. But in the case of a base cumulative sensor that briefly goes Unavailable when it resets to zero at midnight (such as the 7 sensors like `grid_exported_from_battery`, from the Teslemetry integration), there is a problem. Please look at the attached Excel. At midnight, the cumulative sensor shows Unavailable until 00:05, when a valid value is sent. For my example of misbehaviour for `grid_exported_from_battery`, the valid value is 0 as the battery won't export any kWh to the grid until 16:00 Unfortunately, **the Derivative sensor** based on this cumulative sensor **remains Unavailable all day until 16:05**, when a second valid value comes in. **I believe it should show 0 rate of change from 00:05 through 16:00** (rather than Unavailable): there is no updated value in HA, so it can be assumed that the cumulative value is still zero, so the rate of change should be zero. Looking later in the data, we see correct behaviour around 17:00 when the export ends abruptly. The derivative tails off across the 20-minute time window as you might expect. (In reality the power doesn't actually tail off, it stops suddenly, but I understand this representation). And we also see good behaviour after the brief Unavailable periods at 17:31 and 17:37: When the cumulative sensor goes Unavailable, the Derivative goes Unavailable as expected. When the cumulative sensor comes back, with the same value as before, the Derivative is correctly set to zero. This shows that the code doesn't need two valid values after **every** Unavailable period, **just the one at midnight** - so I think the issue may have something to do with the handling of the cumulative sensor's reset to zero being simultaneous with dealing with Unavailable. Unlike an Unavailable period during the day, the code has a previous valid value to fall back on. On the midnight reset, it may have discarded the pre-midnight value when it received the 00:05 zero. Happy to clarify anything if this is not clear.
